topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: LEO satellites allow smaller apertures due to lower FSPL, while GEO requires larger antennas for sufficient gain. Phased arrays and hybrid beamforming enhance spectral efficiency, mitigating aperture size limitations. This trade-off affects portability, network capacity, and interference management, with LEO favoring compactness and GEO prioritizing coverage.
reference_context: SatCom systems involve trade-offs between antenna gain, FSPL, and beam size, with LEO and GEO satellites having distinct requirements.
